🖥 Public commemorations for martyred Leader will continue until Eid al-Fitr: VP

📌 Tehran, IRNA – First Vice President Mohammad-Reza Aref has announced that Iran will hold public commemorative events to mark the first anniversary of the martyrdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, until Eid al-Fitr.

Speaking at a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, Aref congratulated the nation on Basij Week, describing the Basij as a valuable achievement of the Islamic Revolution and highlighting the role of Basij members—particularly specialists—in the country’s development and scientific and technological progress.
​
He stressed the need to preserve the Basij spirit, saying national unity and cohesion are key to the country’s success in confronting its adversaries.
​
Referring to the public commemorations for the martyred Leader, Aref said there had been widespread requests from inside and outside the country to take part in the anniversary events, with spontaneous initiatives already underway.
​
He said a headquarters has been established, in line with the directives of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, to guide and support public participation. Aref stressed that the people would organize the ceremonies primarily, while the anniversary headquarters and government institutions would serve only to coordinate and facilitate their activities.
​
The first vice president further emphasized the importance of using the anniversary ceremonies to highlight the martyred Leader’s personality, intellectual legacy, and views, particularly on science and technology, calling for efforts to implement his guidance and produce cultural and artistic works in line with the event’s objectives.
